pages.text: Great Bodies are the primary nesting places of $(l:offsprings/weaver)$(0)$(n)Weavers$(). They are formed underground and can be found in three main stages of formation: skeletal, muscly, and pseudo-formed. The Great Body resembles an upside down human lacking limbs and can most easily be found by the end of their spine that sticks out at the surface, from which it's possible to descend down into the skull.

pages.title: Skeletal Great Body
pages.text: The skull and the heart are the most valuable parts of it.

pages.title: Addendum
pages.text: The Great Bodies highlight one of the two natures of the joyplague: that of seeking to be alive. Although they are at best horrific caricatures of a human, they can still be recognized as one, which is an achievement of mimicry in itself. I do wonder why exactly part of the Risus is trying to be 'alive', whereas the other part of it is simply maintaining what is already ruined and ashen. Then there's the parts where the two mix

most profanely: organic matter and the offsprings, which help the joyplague form an ecosystem or carve itself a part in the existing one... The more I understand of the Risus the more it seems to me like it's nothing more than a means to an end, like a universal tool that works on anything, either through spreading 'life' or by stabilizing degeneration and decay. But what's the goal and who exactly is using it...? Could it actually be a tool with no wielder?
